# Research question

Standard growth regressions (Dell, Jones and Olken 2012; Burke, Hsiang and
Miguel 2015) find robust effects of temperature but little or no effect of
precipitation. This notebook asks whether that changes when each variable's
deviation from its long-run climate is measured in standard deviations and
positive and negative deviations get separate arms: if dry and wet years both
lower growth, a single slope cancels them out.

1. The standard BHM specification on PWT x ERA5, with and without the conflict
   and collapse controls and the growth outliers.
2. The preferred deviation model on PWT x ERA5: deviation definitions and
   linear or quadratic arms.
3. Its robustness across national panels (PWT, World Bank) and climate datasets
   (ERA5, CRU TS, UDelaware): (a) can the precipitation terms jointly be
   rejected; (b) which arms are significant where; (c) the effect of a +/-3 SD
   deviation in cold (dry), medium and hot (wet) climates.
4. The same model on subnational data (DOSE).
5. The same model in levels: log output per worker, with and without capital
   (PWT x ERA5).

Sample: `r params$start_year` to the last year of each panel. Climate:
population-density weights at base year 2000. Every model has year and unit
fixed effects and unit linear trends (BHM: quadratic trends), with errors
clustered by country.

## Shared specification

```{r shared-specification}
START_YEAR <- as.integer(params$start_year)
CLIMATE_WEIGHT <- "population density"
CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR <- 2000L

OUTCOME <- "dlgrp_pc_usd"
FIXED_EFFECTS <- "year + GID_1 + GID_1[year]"
# BHM (2015): unit fixed effects and unit quadratic trends.
BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS <- "year + GID_1[t, t2]"

# The UCDP/PRIO conflict indicators by the highest intensity of the country's
# conflicts that year (functions/conflict.R): conflict_low, minor (25-999
# battle deaths), and conflict_high, war (1,000 or more); and the post-Soviet
# (with Albania) and post-Yugoslav collapse-year dummies
# (functions/transition_collapse.R). National, so the same for every region of
# a country in the subnational panel.
CONFLICT_TERMS <- c("conflict_low", "conflict_high")
CONTROLS <- c(
  CONFLICT_TERMS,
  "i(fsu_collapse_year, ref = 'none')",
  "i(yug_collapse_year, ref = 'none')"
)

# Growth outliers: the country-years of data/growth_outlier_causes.csv, the 2.5%
# lowest and the 2.5% highest growth rates of GDP per capita of PWT x ERA5 from
# 1960 (growth_outliers.R), each with its likely cause. Dropped: those whose
# cause does not involve weather; the droughts, storms, floods and harvests
# among them are the response studied and stay. They are events of a country
# and year, so they are dropped from every panel (in DOSE, from every region of
# the country).
OUTLIER_SHARE <- 0.05
OUTLIER_CAUSES <- utils::read.csv(data_file("growth_outlier_causes.csv"),
                                  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
OUTLIERS_ALL <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[, c("GID_0", "year")]
OUTLIERS_DROPPED <- OUTLIER_CAUSES[OUTLIER_CAUSES$weather == "no", c("GID_0", "year")]

# Moments of the two deviation definitions: over the horizon of the panel
# (*_all, replaced below) and over the 20 years before the current one.
MOMENTS <- c(
  "mean_TM_all", "sd_TM_all", "mean_RR_all", "sd_RR_all",
  "mean_TM_lag_20", "sd_TM_lag_20", "mean_RR_lag_20", "sd_RR_lag_20"
)

fit_model <- function(terms, model_data, fixed_effects = FIXED_EFFECTS, outcome = OUTCOME) {
  fit_panel_model(
    paste(terms, collapse = " + "),
    model_data,
    outcome = outcome,
    fixed_effects = fixed_effects,
    cluster = ~GID_0
  )
}

# Labels for the coefficient tables; the collapse dummies are left out of them.
DICT <- c(
  TM = "T", TM2 = "T^2", RR = "P", RR2 = "P^2",
  conflict_low = "Conflict, minor", conflict_high = "Conflict, war",
  mean_TM_all = "mean T", mean_RR_all = "mean P",
  devTM = "dT", devTM_pos = "dT+", devTM_neg = "dT-",
  devTM_pos2 = "(dT+)^2", devTM_neg2 = "(dT-)^2",
  devRR = "dP", devRR_pos = "dP+", devRR_neg = "dP-",
  devRR_pos2 = "(dP+)^2", devRR_neg2 = "(dP-)^2"
)
DROP <- "collapse_year"
# Temperature terms, then precipitation terms, then the controls (original names).
ORDER <- c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^conflict")
FITSTAT <- ~n + wr2 + aic + bic
```

## Panels

Each panel runs from `r params$start_year` to its last year with both growth
and climate. `build_dat()` gives each unit's climate moments over its entire
climate series; `mean_*_all` and `sd_*_all` are replaced here by the moments
over the horizon of the panel,

```text
mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all = mean and SD of TM over start year .. last year of the panel
mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all = the same for RR
```

from the climate series of every year in that horizon. The sample is the
unit-years with growth, both weather variables, the conflict indicators and the
moments of both deviation definitions (positive SDs), without the growth
outliers whose cause does not involve weather (see the shared specification).

```{r panel-builder}
# Panel `econ` x `source` from START_YEAR, with the horizon moments, the
# controls, the sample with and without the country-years `drop`, the rows
# dropped, and every unit-year of the panel (`data`, for lags of the weather).
prepare_panel <- function(econ, source, econ_variable = NULL, drop = OUTLIERS_DROPPED) {
  cfg <- panel_config(
    econ_year_min = START_YEAR,
    climate_source = source,
    climate_weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT,
    climate_weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
    # Eleven earlier climate years: up to ten carry the lags of the deviations
    # into the first years, one the lagged trailing moments. The sample starts
    # at START_YEAR regardless.
    clim_history_years = 11L
  )
  data <- suppressMessages(build_dat(econ_data = econ, config = cfg,
                                     econ_variable = econ_variable))
  level <- unique(data$gadm_level)
  end_year <- max(data$year[est_row(data) & !is.na(data$TM) & !is.na(data$RR)])

  horizon <- load_climate_panel(level, cfg) %>%
    filter(gadm_level == level, year >= START_YEAR, year <= end_year) %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_TM_all = mean(TM, na.rm = TRUE), sd_TM_all = sd(TM, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_RR_all = mean(RR, na.rm = TRUE), sd_RR_all = sd(RR, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  data <- data %>%
    select(-c(mean_TM_all, sd_TM_all, mean_RR_all, sd_RR_all)) %>%
    left_join(horizon, by = "GID_1")
  data <- add_yugoslav_collapse(add_soviet_collapse(add_conflict(data)))
  data$TM2 <- data$TM^2
  data$RR2 <- data$RR^2
  data$t <- data$year - 1990L
  data$t2 <- data$t^2

  complete <- stats::complete.cases(
    as.data.frame(data)[, c(OUTCOME, "TM", "RR", CONFLICT_TERMS, MOMENTS)]
  )
  positive_sd <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(grep("^sd_", MOMENTS, value = TRUE), function(x) {
    !is.na(data[[x]]) & data[[x]] > 0
  }))
  sample_all <- data[est_row(data) & data$year >= START_YEAR & complete & positive_sd, ]
  dropped <- paste(sample_all$GID_0, sample_all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  list(
    label = paste(econ, "x", source), econ = econ, source = source, level = level,
    end_year = end_year, all = sample_all, clean = sample_all[!dropped, ],
    outliers = sample_all[dropped, c("GID_0", "GID_1", "year", OUTCOME)], data = data
  )
}

# (The argument is not called `panel`: tibble() would mask it with the column.)
panel_summary <- function(p) {
  tibble::tibble(
    panel = p$label,
    first_year = min(p$clean$year), last_year = max(p$clean$year),
    countries = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_0), units = n_distinct(p$clean$GID_1),
    observations = nrow(p$all), outliers_dropped = nrow(p$outliers),
    minor_conflict = sum(p$clean$conflict_low), war = sum(p$clean$conflict_high)
  )
}

main <- prepare_panel("PWT", "ERA5")

# The outlier country-years are the growth tails of this sample.
cutoffs <- stats::quantile(main$all[[OUTCOME]], c(OUTLIER_SHARE / 2, 1 - OUTLIER_SHARE / 2),
                           names = FALSE)
tails <- main$all[main$all[[OUTCOME]] < cutoffs[[1]] | main$all[[OUTCOME]] > cutoffs[[2]], ]
stopifnot(setequal(paste(tails$GID_0, tails$year),
                   paste(OUTLIERS_ALL$GID_0, OUTLIERS_ALL$year)))

panel_summary(main) %>% knitr::kable(caption = "PWT x ERA5 (unit-years; conflict after outliers)")
OUTLIER_CAUSES %>%
  mutate(tail = ifelse(paste(GID_0, year) %in% paste(tails$GID_0[tails[[OUTCOME]] < 0],
                                                    tails$year[tails[[OUTCOME]] < 0]),
                       "low", "high"),
         status = ifelse(weather == "yes", "kept (weather)", "dropped")) %>%
  count(category, status, tail) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = tail, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(status, desc(low + high)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = sprintf(paste(
    "Growth outliers of PWT x ERA5 (growth below %.1f%% or above %.1f%%) by likely cause;",
    "see data/growth_outlier_causes.csv"), 100 * cutoffs[[1]], 100 * cutoffs[[2]]))
```

# Standard BHM: controls and outliers

The BHM specification in levels, with country fixed effects and country
quadratic trends:

```text
growth = b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 [+ controls] + year + country + country quadratic trend
```

with the two conflict indicators alone, then with the collapse dummies too,
without the outliers, and with both.

```{r bhm}
bhm_terms <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")
BHM_COLUMNS <- c("Baseline", "Conflict", "Conflict + collapse", "Outliers dropped",
                 "Controls, outliers dropped")
m_bhm <- list(
  fit_model(bhm_terms, main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONFLICT_TERMS), main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), main$all, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(bhm_terms, main$clean, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS),
  fit_model(c(bhm_terms, CONTROLS), main$clean, BHM_FIXED_EFFECTS)
)

etable(
  m_bhm,
  headers = BHM_COLUMNS,
  dict = DICT,
  drop = DROP,
  extralines = list(
    "Collapse dummies" = c("No", "No", "Yes", "No", "Yes"),
    "Outliers dropped" = c("No", "No", "No", "Yes", "Yes")
  ),
  fitstat = FITSTAT
)

# The temperature (precipitation) at which its marginal effect is zero,
# -b1 / (2 b2), and the joint Wald tests of each variable's two terms.
tibble::tibble(
  model = BHM_COLUMNS,
  turning_point_T = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) -coef(m)[["TM"]] / (2 * coef(m)[["TM2"]]), 0),
  temperature_p = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^TM2?$", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0),
  turning_point_P = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) -coef(m)[["RR"]] / (2 * coef(m)[["RR2"]]), 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(m_bhm, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^RR2?$", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0)
) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("turning"), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Turning points (C, m) and joint tests of each variable")
```

# Preferred deviation model (PWT x ERA5)

Each variable's deviation from its long-run climate, in SDs, from either of

```text
horizon:  dT = (TM - mean_TM_all) / sd_TM_all            (start year .. last year)
20-year:  dT = (TM - mean_TM_lag_20) / sd_TM_lag_20      (the 20 years before)
```

(the same for precipitation, dP), in four combinations, and three forms of each
variable's deviation, each interacted with its long-run climate (the horizon
mean):

```text
dT+ = max(dT, 0)    dT- = max(-dT, 0)

signed          a dT  + b dT x mean_TM_all
linear arms     a+ dT+ + a- dT- + (b+ dT+ + b- dT-) x mean_TM_all
quadratic arms  a+ (dT+)^2 + a- (dT-)^2 + (b+ (dT+)^2 + b- (dT-)^2) x mean_TM_all
```

(and the same in dP), with the same form for both variables, or linear arms for
one and quadratic arms for the other:

```text
growth = temperature terms + precipitation terms + controls + FE
```

All on the same rows (controls included, outliers dropped). The preferred
model is the arms model (linear, quadratic or mixed arms) with the lowest AIC,
unless the `preferred_definition` and `preferred_form` parameters set it.

```{r deviation-helpers}
# Deviation terms against mean_<v>_<suffix> and sd_<v>_<suffix>, with one
# suffix per variable, e.g. c(TM = "all", RR = "lag_20"). The same column
# names under any definition, so the tables line up.
add_deviation_terms <- function(model_data, suffix) {
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) {
    dev <- (model_data[[v]] - model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]) /
      model_data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", suffix[[v]])]]
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]] <- dev
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(dev, 0)^2
    model_data[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-dev, 0)^2
  }
  model_data
}

DEFINITIONS <- list(
  "Horizon" = c(TM = "all", RR = "all"),
  "20-year" = c(TM = "lag_20", RR = "lag_20"),
  "T horizon, P 20-year" = c(TM = "all", RR = "lag_20"),
  "T 20-year, P horizon" = c(TM = "lag_20", RR = "all")
)
# Each form: the deviation terms of each variable, by column suffix.
SIGNED <- ""
LINEAR <- c("_pos", "_neg")
QUADRATIC <- c("_pos2", "_neg2")
FORMS <- list(
  "Signed" = list(TM = SIGNED, RR = SIGNED),
  "Linear arms" = list(TM = LINEAR, RR = LINEAR),
  "Quadratic arms" = list(TM = QUADRATIC, RR = QUADRATIC),
  "T linear, P quadratic arms" = list(TM = LINEAR, RR = QUADRATIC),
  "T quadratic, P linear arms" = list(TM = QUADRATIC, RR = LINEAR)
)
ARMS <- setdiff(names(FORMS), "Signed")

form_terms <- function(form) {
  terms <- unlist(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    x <- paste0("dev", v, form[[v]])
    c(x, paste0(x, ":mean_", v, "_all"))
  }))
  c(terms, CONTROLS)
}

# Value of a deviation term (by column suffix) at deviations x.
term_value <- function(suffix, x) {
  if (suffix == "") return(x)
  switch(suffix, "_pos" = pmax(x, 0), "_neg" = pmax(-x, 0),
         "_pos2" = pmax(x, 0)^2, "_neg2" = pmax(-x, 0)^2)
}
interaction_name <- function(a, b, terms) {
  intersect(c(paste0(a, ":", b), paste0(b, ":", a)), terms)[[1]]
}

# Fit of each model (all on the same rows) and the joint Wald tests of each
# variable's terms.
fit_summary <- function(models) {
  tibble::tibble(
    form = names(models),
    observations = vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0),
    within_r2 = vapply(models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]], 0),
    aic = vapply(models, stats::AIC, 0),
    bic = vapply(models, stats::BIC, 0),
    temperature_p = vapply(models, function(m) {
      fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devTM", print = FALSE)$p
    }, 0),
    precipitation_p = vapply(models, function(m) {
      fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devRR", print = FALSE)$p
    }, 0)
  )
}
```

```{r model-selection}
selection_models <- lapply(DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, def)
  lapply(FORMS, function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
})
selection <- bind_rows(lapply(names(selection_models), function(def) {
  fit_summary(selection_models[[def]]) %>% mutate(definition = def, .before = 1)
}))
stopifnot(length(unique(selection$observations)) == 1)

best_arms <- selection %>% filter(form %in% ARMS) %>% slice_min(aic, n = 1)
PREFERRED_DEFINITION <- if (params$preferred_definition == "auto") {
  best_arms$definition
} else {
  params$preferred_definition
}
PREFERRED_FORM <- if (params$preferred_form == "auto") best_arms$form else params$preferred_form
stopifnot(PREFERRED_DEFINITION %in% names(DEFINITIONS), PREFERRED_FORM %in% ARMS)
PREFERRED_SUFFIX <- DEFINITIONS[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]]

selection %>%
  mutate(
    aic_vs_best = aic - min(aic), bic_vs_best = bic - min(bic),
    preferred = definition == PREFERRED_DEFINITION & form == PREFERRED_FORM,
    within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4),
    across(c(aic, bic, aic_vs_best, bic_vs_best), ~ round(.x, 1)),
    across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))
  ) %>%
  select(-observations) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x ERA5, ", nrow(main$clean), " country-years: fit and ",
                                "joint tests of each variable; AIC and BIC relative to the best ",
                                "of all the models"))
```

Preferred model: **`r PREFERRED_FORM`**, with the **`r PREFERRED_DEFINITION`**
deviations (temperature against mean_TM_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["TM"]]`, precipitation
against mean_RR_`r PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["RR"]]`).

```{r preferred-table}
# Short headers: etable cuts long ones.
SHORT_FORM_NAMES <- c("Signed" = "Signed", "Linear arms" = "Linear", "Quadratic arms" = "Quadratic",
                      "T linear, P quadratic arms" = "T lin, P quad",
                      "T quadratic, P linear arms" = "T quad, P lin")
etable(unname(selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]]),
       headers = unname(SHORT_FORM_NAMES[names(FORMS)]), dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT, title = paste("Deviations:", PREFERRED_DEFINITION))
```

## Binned response of the preferred model

The preferred deviations by quarter of the long-run climate (the quartiles of
`mean_TM_all` and `mean_RR_all` over the sample):

- bins: 0.5 SD bins of the deviation within each quarter, centred on zero, with
  the tails pooled until they hold 10 countries; the bin containing zero is the
  quarter's reference. One model per variable: its bins, the other variable in
  signed + quadratic arms (interacted with its long-run mean), and the controls;
- curves: the signed and preferred forms, estimated once on the whole sample
  (no quarter terms) and evaluated at the quarter's mean long-run climate,
  relative to their mean over the quarter's reference-bin observations.

```{r binned-helpers}
BIN_WIDTH <- 0.5
MIN_COUNTRIES <- 10L
VARIABLE_LABELS <- c(TM = "Temperature", RR = "Precipitation")
QUARTER_NAMES <- list(TM = c("coldest", "cool", "warm", "hottest"),
                      RR = c("driest", "dry", "wet", "wettest"))
CLIMATE_UNITS <- c(TM = "°C", RR = "m")
CLIMATE_DIGITS <- c(TM = 1L, RR = 2L)
# The other variable's terms in the bin models: signed + quadratic arms.
ENCOMPASSING <- c("", "_pos2", "_neg2")
wrap_text <- function(x, width) paste(strwrap(x, width = width), collapse = "\n")

# Quarter of each variable's long-run climate and bins of its deviation within
# each quarter (ids "<quarter>_<index>"), with each bin's size and mean deviation.
add_quarter_bins <- function(model_data) {
  quarters <- list()
  bins <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    climate <- model_data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_all")]]
    breaks <- stats::quantile(climate, seq(0, 1, 0.25), names = FALSE)
    quarter <- as.integer(cut(climate, breaks, include.lowest = TRUE))
    dev <- model_data[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    k_max <- ceiling((max(abs(dev)) + BIN_WIDTH / 2) / BIN_WIDTH)
    edges <- seq(-BIN_WIDTH / 2 - k_max * BIN_WIDTH, BIN_WIDTH / 2 + k_max * BIN_WIDTH,
                 by = BIN_WIDTH)
    bin <- character(nrow(model_data))
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- quarter == q
      q_breaks <- pool_tails(dev[rows], edges, model_data$GID_0[rows], MIN_COUNTRIES)
      bin[rows] <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(dev[rows], q_breaks,
                                                        include.lowest = TRUE)))
      reference <- sprintf("%d_%02d", q, as.integer(cut(0, q_breaks)))
      bins[[length(bins) + 1]] <- tibble::tibble(
        variable = v, quarter = q, bin = bin[rows], deviation = dev[rows],
        GID_0 = model_data$GID_0[rows]
      ) %>%
        group_by(variable, quarter, bin) %>%
        summarise(observations = n(), countries = n_distinct(GID_0),
                  mean_deviation = mean(deviation), .groups = "drop") %>%
        mutate(reference = bin == !!reference)
    }
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] <- quarter
    model_data[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] <- bin
    fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = CLIMATE_DIGITS[[v]])
    # Outside tibble(), whose `quarter` column would mask the vector.
    mean_climate <- as.numeric(tapply(climate, quarter, mean))
    quarters[[v]] <- tibble::tibble(
      variable = v, quarter = 1:4, mean_climate = mean_climate,
      label = sprintf("%s, %s quarter\n%s to %s %s; curves at the mean, %s %s",
                      VARIABLE_LABELS[[v]], QUARTER_NAMES[[v]], fmt(breaks[-5]),
                      fmt(breaks[-1]), CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]], fmt(mean_climate),
                      CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]])
    )
  }
  list(data = model_data, quarters = bind_rows(quarters), bins = bind_rows(bins))
}

# Effect of the interacted form with `suffixes` of variable v at long-run
# climate m and deviations `devs`, relative to its mean over `ref_devs`.
form_curve <- function(model, v, suffixes, m, devs, ref_devs) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  G <- t(vapply(devs, function(x) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    for (s in suffixes) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      value <- term_value(s, x) - mean(term_value(s, ref_devs))
      w[[term]] <- value
      w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("mean_", v, "_all"), terms)]] <- value * m
    }
    w
  }, numeric(length(terms))))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(model, G) %>% mutate(deviation = devs)
}

# Bins by quarter of long-run climate against the interacted `forms`, both
# variables, on common axes.
plot_binned_response <- function(model_data, forms, title, note, caption) {
  qb <- add_quarter_bins(model_data)
  d <- qb$data
  models <- lapply(FORMS[forms], function(s) fit_model(form_terms(s), d))
  bins <- list()
  curves <- list()
  for (v in names(VARIABLE_LABELS)) {
    other <- setdiff(names(VARIABLE_LABELS), v)
    other_terms <- paste0("dev", other, ENCOMPASSING)
    references <- qb$bins %>% filter(variable == v, reference) %>% pull(bin)
    bin_term <- sprintf("i(%s_bin, ref = c(%s))", v,
                        paste0("'", references, "'", collapse = ", "))
    m_bins <- fit_model(c(bin_term, other_terms,
                          paste0(other_terms, ":mean_", other, "_all"), CONTROLS), d)
    prefix <- paste0(v, "_bin::")
    estimates <- tidy_fixest(m_bins) %>%
      filter(startsWith(term, prefix)) %>%
      mutate(bin = sub(prefix, "", term, fixed = TRUE))
    bins[[v]] <- qb$bins %>%
      filter(variable == v) %>%
      left_join(select(estimates, bin, estimate, conf_low, conf_high), by = "bin") %>%
      mutate(across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ ifelse(reference, 0, .x)))

    dev <- d[[paste0("dev", v)]]
    for (q in 1:4) {
      rows <- d[[paste0(v, "_quarter")]] == q
      ref_devs <- dev[rows & d[[paste0(v, "_bin")]] %in% references]
      grid <- seq(min(dev[rows]), max(dev[rows]), length.out = 100)
      m <- qb$quarters$mean_climate[qb$quarters$variable == v & qb$quarters$quarter == q]
      for (f in names(models)) {
        curves[[length(curves) + 1]] <-
          form_curve(models[[f]], v, FORMS[[f]][[v]], m, grid, ref_devs) %>%
          mutate(variable = v, quarter = q, form = f)
      }
    }
  }

  facet_of <- function(variable, quarter) {
    factor(qb$quarters$label[match(paste(variable, quarter),
                                   paste(qb$quarters$variable, qb$quarters$quarter))],
           levels = qb$quarters$label)
  }
  bins <- bind_rows(bins) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))
  curves <- bind_rows(curves) %>%
    mutate(facet = facet_of(variable, quarter), form = factor(form, levels = names(models)),
           across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x))

  ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_line(data = curves, aes(deviation, estimate, colour = form), linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_linerange(data = filter(bins, !reference),
                   aes(mean_deviation, ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high),
                   colour = GRID_INK, linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_point(data = bins, aes(mean_deviation, estimate, shape = reference),
               colour = GRID_INK, fill = "white", size = 2.2) +
    # Common axes across all panels.
    facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(names(FORMS))[names(models)], name = NULL) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 21),
                       labels = c(`FALSE` = "Deviation bin (95% CI)", `TRUE` = "Reference bin"),
                       name = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, order = 1), shape = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    labs(
      x = "Deviation (SD)",
      y = "Effect on growth that year (pp), relative to the reference bin",
      title = title,
      subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
        note, " Top: temperature, by quarter of long-run temperature; bottom: ",
        "precipitation, by quarter of long-run precipitation. Bins of ", BIN_WIDTH,
        " SD centred on zero (points at the bin's mean deviation; tails pooled to ",
        MIN_COUNTRIES, " countries). Curves: the forms interacted with the long-run ",
        "climate, estimated on the whole sample and evaluated at the quarter's mean ",
        "long-run climate, relative to the reference bin. Common axes."), 175),
      caption = wrap_text(caption, 175)
    ) +
    theme_results()
}

panel_caption <- function(panel) {
  paste0(panel$label, ", ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT, " ", CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR, " weights, ",
         min(panel$clean$year), "-", max(panel$clean$year), "; controls: conflict ",
         "(minor, war), post-Soviet and post-Yugoslav collapse dummies; ",
         nrow(panel$outliers), " growth outliers not involving weather dropped. ",
         "Fixed effects year + unit + unit linear trends; ",
         "errors clustered by country.")
}
```

```{r binned-preferred, fig.width=15, fig.height=8.5}
  forms = c("Signed", PREFERRED_FORM),
  title = paste0("PWT x ERA5, ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations: bins against signed and ",
                 tolower(PREFERRED_FORM)),
  note = paste0("dT from mean_TM_", PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["TM"]], ", dP from mean_RR_",
                PREFERRED_SUFFIX[["RR"]], " (in the matching SDs)."),
```

# Robustness across national and climate datasets

The preferred model (and the signed form, for comparison) on every national
panel: PWT and World Bank GDP per capita (both at constant prices) with ERA5,
CRU TS and UDelaware climate. Each panel has its own horizon, long-run
climate, sample and outliers.

- (a) Joint Wald tests of all temperature terms and of all precipitation terms
  of the preferred model, and of the precipitation terms of the signed form.
- (b) and (c) The effect of a deviation of +3 SD and of -3 SD, against a normal
  year, for a unit with a long-run temperature of 5, 15 or 25 °C and a
  long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 or 3 m a year. With arms, the +3 SD effect
  depends only on the positive arm and the -3 SD effect only on the negative
  one, so (b) is which of these effects are significant. The range of the
  long-run climate across the units of each panel shows how far inside the
  data each of these climates is.

```{r robustness-helpers}
# Deviations (SD) and long-run climates (C, m a year) at which the effects are
# evaluated.
EFFECT_AT <- c(-3, 3)
EVAL_CLIMATE <- list(TM = c(5, 15, 25), RR = c(0.5, 1.5, 3))
EVAL_LABELS <- list(TM = c("5 °C", "15 °C", "25 °C"), RR = c("0.5 m", "1.5 m", "3 m"))

# The preferred and signed models on a panel, with its deviation data.
fit_robustness <- function(panel) {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(panel$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  list(
    panel = panel, data = d,
    preferred = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]]), d),
    signed = fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[["Signed"]]), d)
  )
}

# (a) joint tests.
joint_tests <- function(fit) {
  wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p
  panel_summary(fit$panel) %>%
    select(panel, first_year, last_year, countries, units, outliers_dropped) %>%
    mutate(
      observations = stats::nobs(fit$preferred),
      temperature_p = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"),
      precipitation_p = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"),
      precipitation_p_signed = wald_p(fit$signed, "^devRR"),
      aic_vs_signed = stats::AIC(fit$preferred) - stats::AIC(fit$signed)
    )
}

# (b), (c) effect of a deviation of EFFECT_AT SD of each variable at each
# long-run climate of EVAL_CLIMATE, with delta-method CIs (clustered by country).
climate_effects <- function(fit) {
  model <- fit$preferred
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    m <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), deviation = EFFECT_AT)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]]) {
        term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
        w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
        w[[interaction_name(term, paste0("mean_", v, "_all"), terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * m[[g]]
      }
      w
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(panel = fit$panel$label, variable = v, level_index = grid$level,
             level = factor(EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], levels = EVAL_LABELS[[v]]),
             climate = m[grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}

stars <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.01, "***", ifelse(p < 0.05, "**", ifelse(p < 0.1, "*", "")))

# (b) one row per panel: each effect with its significance.
significance_map <- function(effects) {
  effects %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value)),
           column = sprintf("%s %+d SD, %s", ifelse(variable == "TM", "T", "P"),
                            deviation, level)) %>%
    select(panel, column, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell)
}

# (c) one table per variable: rows panel x deviation, columns long-run
# climates, effect [95% CI] in pp.
effects_table <- function(effects, v) {
  effects %>%
    filter(variable == v) %>%
    mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f [%+.2f, %+.2f]%s", 100 * estimate, 100 * conf_low,
                          100 * conf_high, stars(p_value)),
           deviation = sprintf("%+d SD", deviation)) %>%
    select(panel, deviation, level, cell) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = cell) %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel))) %>%
    arrange(panel, deviation)
}

# Range of the long-run climate across the units (countries or regions) of
# each panel.
climate_support <- function(fits) {
  bind_rows(lapply(fits, function(fit) {
    units <- distinct(fit$data, GID_1, mean_TM_all, mean_RR_all)
    bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
      q <- stats::quantile(units[[paste0("mean_", v, "_all")]], c(0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1),
                           names = FALSE)
      tibble::tibble(panel = fit$panel$label,
                     variable = paste0(VARIABLE_LABELS[[v]], " (", CLIMATE_UNITS[[v]], ")"),
                     units = nrow(units), min = q[1], p10 = q[2], median = q[3], p90 = q[4],
                     max = q[5])
    }))
  })) %>%
    mutate(across(c(min, p10, median, p90, max), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
    arrange(variable)
}

PLOT_COLUMNS <- paste(EVAL_LABELS$TM, "/", EVAL_LABELS$RR)
plot_effects <- function(effects, title) {
  effects %>%
    mutate(
      row = factor(sprintf("%s, %+d SD", VARIABLE_LABELS[variable], deviation),
                   levels = c("Temperature, +3 SD", "Temperature, -3 SD",
                              "Precipitation, +3 SD", "Precipitation, -3 SD")),
      column = factor(PLOT_COLUMNS[level_index], levels = PLOT_COLUMNS),
      panel = factor(panel, levels = rev(unique(panel))),
      across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x)
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(estimate, panel)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_linerange(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]],
                   linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(colour = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], size = 2) +
    facet_grid(row ~ column) +
    labs(x = "Effect on growth that year (pp), against a normal year; 95% CI", y = NULL,
         title = title,
         subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations; at ",
                           "long-run climates of 5, 15 and 25 °C (temperature) and 0.5, 1.5 ",
                           "and 3 m a year (precipitation).")) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e6e5df", linewidth = 0.3))
}
```

```{r robustness-national}
NATIONAL <- expand.grid(source = c("ERA5", "CRU TS", "UDelaware"), econ = c("PWT", "WB"),
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
national_panels <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(NATIONAL)), function(i) {
  if (NATIONAL$econ[i] == "PWT" && NATIONAL$source[i] == "ERA5") return(main)
  prepare_panel(NATIONAL$econ[i], NATIONAL$source[i])
})
national_fits <- lapply(national_panels, fit_robustness)
national_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(national_fits, climate_effects))

bind_rows(lapply(national_fits, joint_tests)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(temperature_p, precipitation_p, precipitation_p_signed), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         aic_vs_signed = round(aic_vs_signed, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(a) Joint Wald tests of the preferred model (temperature,",
                               "precipitation) and of the signed form (precipitation); AIC of the",
                               "preferred model minus the signed form"))

significance_map(national_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(b) Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation at long-run climates of 5, 15,",
                               "25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m (pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

climate_support(national_fits) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Long-run climate across the countries of each panel")

effects_table(national_effects, "TM") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(c) Temperature: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI) at",
                               "long-run temperatures of 5, 15 and 25 °C"))
effects_table(national_effects, "RR") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(c) Precipitation: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI) at",
                               "long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 and 3 m a year"))
```

# Subnational data (DOSE)

The same model on DOSE v2.14 regional GDP per capita (GADM1) with ERA5 climate
(population-density weights at base year 2000, aggregated to the regions):
GDP per capita at constant 2015 local prices converted at the fixed 2015
exchange rate (`lcu2015_usd`; its growth is constant-local-price growth, free
of exchange-rate movements). Region fixed effects and region linear trends;
the conflict and collapse controls are national; the dropped outliers are the
national country-years of the shared specification, dropped in every region of
the country; errors are clustered by country.

```{r subnational}
dose <- prepare_panel("DOSE", "ERA5", econ_variable = params$dose_variable)
dose_fit <- fit_robustness(dose)
dose_effects <- climate_effects(dose_fit)

joint_tests(dose_fit) %>%
  mutate(across(c(temperature_p, precipitation_p, precipitation_p_signed), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         aic_vs_signed = round(aic_vs_signed, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "(a) DOSE x ERA5: joint Wald tests")

etable(list("Signed" = dose_fit$signed, "Preferred" = dose_fit$preferred), dict = DICT,
       drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT, title = "DOSE x ERA5")

significance_map(dose_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("(b) DOSE x ERA5: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation at long-run",
                               "climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m (pp); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
climate_support(list(dose_fit)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Long-run climate across the DOSE regions")
effects_table(dose_effects, "TM") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "(c) DOSE x ERA5, temperature: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI)")
effects_table(dose_effects, "RR") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "(c) DOSE x ERA5, precipitation: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp, 95% CI)")
```

# Level model: output per worker and capital (PWT x ERA5)

The preferred model with the log level of output per worker as the outcome,
without capital, with log capital per worker (the intensive form of a
production function), and with log capital and log employment separately:

```text
log(Y/L) = deviation terms (preferred model) + controls
           [ + c log(K/L) ]  or  [ + c1 log K + c2 log L ]  + year + country + country trend
```

with `Y` real GDP and `K` the capital stock, both at constant national prices
(PWT `rgdpna`, `rnna`), and `L` persons engaged (`emp`), all in the same year.
Constant returns to scale in the last column mean `c2 = -c1`. With capital, the
deviation terms are the effect on output given the capital stock (labour
and productivity); without, the total. The growth model on the same rows is
the reference. Rows: the PWT x ERA5 sample (outliers dropped) with employment
and capital.

```{r level-model}
# Output, capital and employment from PWT 11.0 (millions of 2021 US$ at constant
# national prices; millions of persons engaged).
pwt_levels <- readxl::read_excel(data_file(ECON_RAW_FILES[["PWT110"]]), sheet = "Data") %>%
  transmute(GID_0 = as.character(countrycode), year = as.integer(year),
            rgdpna = as.numeric(rgdpna), rnna = as.numeric(rnna), emp = as.numeric(emp)) %>%
  filter(rgdpna > 0, rnna > 0, emp > 0) %>%
  transmute(GID_0, year, log_y_worker = log(rgdpna / emp), log_k_worker = log(rnna / emp),
            log_k = log(rnna), log_emp = log(emp))
level_data <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
  inner_join(pwt_levels, by = c("GID_0", "year"))

preferred_terms <- form_terms(FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]])
m_level <- list(
  "Growth" = fit_model(preferred_terms, level_data),
  "Level" = fit_model(preferred_terms, level_data, outcome = "log_y_worker"),
  "Level, K/L" = fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "log_k_worker"), level_data,
                           outcome = "log_y_worker"),
  "Level, K, L" = fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "log_k", "log_emp"), level_data,
                            outcome = "log_y_worker")
)
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(m_level, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

LEVEL_DICT <- c(DICT, log_k_worker = "log K/L", log_k = "log K", log_emp = "log L")
etable(m_level, dict = LEVEL_DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^log_k_worker$", "%^log_k$", "%^log_emp$", ORDER), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       notes = paste("Outcome: growth of GDP per capita (first column), log GDP per worker",
                     "(the others)."))

tibble::tibble(
  model = names(m_level),
  observations = vapply(m_level, stats::nobs, 0),
  countries = n_distinct(level_data$GID_0),
  temperature_p = vapply(m_level, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devTM", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(m_level, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devRR", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0),
  # Constant returns to scale: c1 + c2 = 0.
  constant_returns_p = c(NA, NA, NA, lincom(m_level[["Level, K, L"]],
                                            c(log_k = 1, log_emp = 1))$p_value)
) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint tests of each variable's deviation terms, and of constant returns")

level_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(m_level), function(k) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = m_level[[k]], panel = list(label = k)))
}))
significance_map(level_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation at long-run climates of 5, 15,",
                               "25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m: growth (pp, first row), level of output",
                               "per worker (%, the others); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

## Growth with capital accumulation

The preferred growth model with the growth of capital per capita, of the same
year or of the year before, and with the growth of the employment share (a
growth-accounting decomposition):

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + controls
         [ + a dlog(K/N) ]  or  [ + a dlog(K/N)(t-1) ]  or  [ + a dlog(K/N) + b dlog(L/N) ] + FE
```

with `N` population and `L` persons engaged (PWT `pop`, `emp`). The capital
stock of a year includes that year's investment, which can respond to the
same weather, so the same-year capital growth may absorb part of the weather
effect (it is partly an outcome); the previous year's is set before the
weather. With capital growth, the deviation terms are the effect on growth
given capital deepening (labour and productivity). All columns on the same
rows.

```{r growth-capital}
pwt_growth <- readxl::read_excel(data_file(ECON_RAW_FILES[["PWT110"]]), sheet = "Data") %>%
  transmute(GID_0 = as.character(countrycode), year = as.integer(year),
            rnna = as.numeric(rnna), pop = as.numeric(pop), emp = as.numeric(emp)) %>%
  filter(rnna > 0, pop > 0) %>%
  arrange(GID_0, year) %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  mutate(
    log_k_pc = log(rnna / pop),
    dlk_pc = log_k_pc - lag_by_year(log_k_pc, year),
    dlk_pc_lag = lag_by_year(dlk_pc, year),
    log_emp_pop = log(ifelse(emp > 0, emp / pop, NA_real_)),
    dl_emp_pop = log_emp_pop - lag_by_year(log_emp_pop, year)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(GID_0, year, dlk_pc, dlk_pc_lag, dl_emp_pop)
growth_data <- add_deviation_terms(main$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
  inner_join(pwt_growth, by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dlk_pc), !is.na(dlk_pc_lag), !is.na(dl_emp_pop))

m_growth_k <- list(
  "Growth" = fit_model(preferred_terms, growth_data),
  "+ dk" = fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "dlk_pc"), growth_data),
  "+ dk(t-1)" = fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "dlk_pc_lag"), growth_data),
  "+ dk, dl" = fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "dlk_pc", "dl_emp_pop"), growth_data)
)
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(m_growth_k, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

GROWTH_DICT <- c(DICT, dlk_pc = "dlog(K/N)", dlk_pc_lag = "dlog(K/N)(t-1)",
                 dl_emp_pop = "dlog(L/N)")
etable(m_growth_k, dict = GROWTH_DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^dlk_pc$", "%^dlk_pc_lag$", "%^dl_emp_pop$", ORDER), fitstat = FITSTAT)

tibble::tibble(
  model = names(m_growth_k),
  observations = vapply(m_growth_k, stats::nobs, 0),
  temperature_p = vapply(m_growth_k, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devTM", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(m_growth_k, function(m) {
    fixest::wald(m, keep = "^devRR", print = FALSE)$p
  }, 0)
) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint tests of each variable's deviation terms")

growth_k_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(m_growth_k), function(k) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = m_growth_k[[k]], panel = list(label = k)))
}))
significance_map(growth_k_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation on growth (pp) at long-run",
                               "climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m; *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Preferred model and the BHM level terms

The preferred model with the BHM level terms added, on every panel (the same
fixed effects as the preferred model: unit linear trends):

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 + controls + FE
```

Does each block still matter given the other? Joint Wald tests of the deviation
terms of each variable and of its BHM terms, alone and together, and the AIC of
the combined model against each alone. In the combined model a deviation of
the year also moves `TM` and `TM^2` (or `RR`, `RR^2`), so its effect is not
the deviation terms alone; the joint tests and the AIC are the comparison.

```{r bhm-preferred}
BHM_TERMS <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")
wald_p <- function(m, pattern) fixest::wald(m, keep = pattern, print = FALSE)$p

bhm_comparison <- function(fit) {
  d <- fit$data
  m_bhm <- fit_model(c(BHM_TERMS, CONTROLS), d)
  m_both <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, BHM_TERMS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m_bhm) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred),
            stats::nobs(m_both) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  list(
    models = list("BHM" = m_bhm, "Preferred" = fit$preferred, "Preferred + BHM" = m_both),
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      dev_T_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"),
      dev_T_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devTM"),
      bhm_T_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^TM2?$"),
      bhm_T_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^TM2?$"),
      dev_P_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"),
      dev_P_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devRR"),
      bhm_P_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^RR2?$"),
      bhm_P_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^RR2?$"),
      aic_vs_preferred = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(fit$preferred),
      aic_vs_bhm = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(m_bhm)
    )
  )
}

bhm_comparisons <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), bhm_comparison)

etable(bhm_comparisons[[1]]$models, dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^TM$", "%^TM2$", "%^RR$", "%^RR2$", ORDER), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = main$label)

bind_rows(lapply(bhm_comparisons, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("dev_"), starts_with("bhm_")), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Joint Wald tests (p) of the deviation terms (dev) and of the BHM",
                               "terms (bhm) of each variable, alone and with the other block;",
                               "AIC of the combined model minus each alone"))
```

# Preferred model and lagged income

The preferred model with the previous year's log GDP per capita, on every
panel:

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + h log(GDP per capita)(t-1) + controls + FE
```

With unit fixed effects and trends, `h` is mostly mean reversion within units
(and has the small-T bias of a lagged level with unit effects). Do the
deviation terms survive it?

```{r lagged-income}
lagged_income <- function(fit) {
  d <- mutate(fit$data, lag_log_gdp_pc = lgrp_pc_usd - dlgrp_pc_usd)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "lag_log_gdp_pc"), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)
  list(
    model = m,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      lag_gdp = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 1], lag_gdp_se = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 2],
      within_r2_without = fixest::fitstat(fit$preferred, "wr2")[[1]],
      within_r2_with = fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]],
      T_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"), T_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
      P_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"), P_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devRR")
    )
  )
}

income_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), lagged_income)

bind_rows(lapply(income_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(lag_gdp, lag_gdp_se, within_r2_without, within_r2_with), ~ round(.x, 4)),
         across(ends_with("_without") | ends_with("_with"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Lagged log GDP per capita: its coefficient, the within R2 and the",
                               "joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms without and",
                               "with it"))

income_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(income_fits), function(i) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = income_fits[[i]]$model,
                       panel = list(label = income_fits[[i]]$tests$panel)))
}))
significance_map(income_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("With lagged log GDP per capita: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation",
                               "(pp) at long-run climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Lags of the deviations

Instead of lagged income, the deviation terms of the previous five years, in
the same forms and interacted with the same long-run climate, for both
variables:

```text
growth = sum over k = 0..5 of [ temperature terms(t-k) + precipitation terms(t-k) ] + controls + FE
```

The lags are the deviations of the calendar years before (from every year of
the panel, whether or not it has growth), so a unit-year enters only with all
five lags. The cumulative effect of a deviation through year K is the sum of
its effects on growth in years 0..K, i.e. its effect on the level of GDP per
capita after K years: if a loss is recovered it returns towards zero, if it
persists it stays. The model without lags is re-estimated on the same rows.

Two versions:

- unrestricted: every lag has its own arm coefficients and its own
  interactions with the long-run climate (8 coefficients a lag);
- common interaction: every lag has its own arm coefficients, but each arm has
  one interaction with the long-run climate shared by all lags,

  ```text
  sum over k of [ a+_k dT+(t-k) + a-_k dT-(t-k) ]
    + b+ (sum over k of dT+(t-k)) x mean_TM_all + b- (sum over k of dT-(t-k)) x mean_TM_all
  ```

  (and the same for precipitation), so the effect of lag k at long-run climate
  m is `a_k + b m`: the climate shifts the response equally in every year.
  The test of the restriction is the joint (chi-square) Wald test, in the
  unrestricted model, that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag.

```{r deviation-lags}
N_LAGS <- 5L
lag_suffix <- function(k) if (k == 0) "" else paste0("_l", k)

# Columns of the deviation terms of variable v in the preferred form.
form_columns <- function(v) paste0("dev", v, FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]])

# Unrestricted: the deviation terms of variable v at lag k, with their
# interactions.
lag_terms <- function(v, k) {
  x <- paste0(form_columns(v), lag_suffix(k))
  c(x, paste0(x, ":mean_", v, "_all"))
}
# Common interaction: the terms of variable v at lags 1..n_lags (lag 0 is in
# the preferred model, without its interaction), and each arm's sum over lags
# 0..n_lags interacted with the long-run climate.
restricted_terms <- function(v, n_lags = N_LAGS) {
  cols <- form_columns(v)
  c(cols, unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_lags), function(k) paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k)))),
    paste0(cols, "_sum:mean_", v, "_all"))
}

# The sample of a fit with the deviations of the previous n_lags calendar years,
# on the unit-years with all of them, and each arm's sum over lags 0..n_lags.
add_deviation_lags <- function(fit, n_lags = N_LAGS) {
  full <- add_deviation_terms(fit$panel$data, PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  cols <- c(form_columns("TM"), form_columns("RR"))
  out <- fit$data
  for (k in seq_len(n_lags)) {
    lagged <- as.data.frame(full)[, c("GID_1", "year", cols)]
    lagged$year <- lagged$year + k
    names(lagged)[-(1:2)] <- paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k))
    out <- left_join(out, lagged, by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  }
  lag_cols <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(n_lags), function(k) paste0(cols, lag_suffix(k))))
  # Finite, not only present: a zero trailing SD gives an infinite deviation.
  out <- out[Reduce(`&`, lapply(lag_cols, function(x) is.finite(out[[x]]))), ]
  for (col in cols) {
    out[[paste0(col, "_sum")]] <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(0:n_lags, function(k) {
      out[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]]
    }))
  }
  out
}

# Chi-square Wald test of H b = 0 (clustered VCOV of the model).
wald_linear_p <- function(model, H) {
  b <- stats::coef(model)[colnames(H)]
  V <- stats::vcov(model)[colnames(H), colnames(H)]
  r <- H %*% b
  stat <- as.numeric(t(r) %*% solve(H %*% V %*% t(H)) %*% r)
  stats::pchisq(stat, df = nrow(H), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
# In the unrestricted model: each arm of the variables `vars` has the same
# interaction at every lag (b_k = b_0 for k = 1..N_LAGS).
equal_interactions_p <- function(model, vars) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  rows <- list()
  for (v in vars) for (col in form_columns(v)) {
    climate <- paste0("mean_", v, "_all")
    base <- interaction_name(col, climate, terms)
    for (k in seq_len(N_LAGS)) {
      h <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      h[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), climate, terms)]] <- 1
      h[[base]] <- -1
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- h
    }
  }
  wald_linear_p(model, do.call(rbind, rows))
}

distributed_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit)
  all_lags <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(N_LAGS), function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, all_lags), d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM"), restricted_terms("RR"), CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(m), stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, no_lags = m0, lags = m, restricted = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(m),
      T_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devTM"), P_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devRR"),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      T_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      P_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      equal_T_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "TM"), equal_P_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "RR"),
      aic_lags_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(m0),
      aic_common_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0)
    )
  )
}

# Cumulative effect through year `through` of a deviation of EFFECT_AT SD in
# year 0, at each long-run climate of EVAL_CLIMATE. With the common interaction
# (`restricted`), the deviation enters the summed interaction in each of the
# years 0..through.
cumulative_effects <- function(model, label, restricted = FALSE, n_lags = N_LAGS) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    m <- EVAL_CLIMATE[[v]]
    climate <- paste0("mean_", v, "_all")
    grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), deviation = EFFECT_AT, through = 0:n_lags)
    G <- t(mapply(function(g, x, through) {
      w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][[v]]) {
        value <- term_value(s, x)
        col <- paste0("dev", v, s)
        for (k in 0:through) w[[paste0(col, lag_suffix(k))]] <- value
        if (restricted) {
          w[[interaction_name(paste0(col, "_sum"), climate, terms)]] <- (through + 1) * value * m[[g]]
        } else {
          for (k in 0:through) {
            w[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), climate, terms)]] <- value * m[[g]]
          }
        }
      }
      w
    }, grid$level, grid$deviation, grid$through))
    colnames(G) <- terms
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(panel = label, variable = v, level_index = grid$level,
             level = factor(EVAL_LABELS[[v]][grid$level], levels = EVAL_LABELS[[v]]),
             climate = m[grid$level], deviation = grid$deviation, through = grid$through,
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)), .before = 1)
  }))
}

lag_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), distributed_lags)
lag_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$lags, x$panel$label)
}))
common_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$restricted, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE)
}))

lag_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("T_"), starts_with("P_"), starts_with("equal_")),
                ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1)))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, first_year, observations, T_p_no_lags, P_p_no_lags, T_lags_p, P_lags_p,
         aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: joint tests (p) of the deviation terms without",
                               "lags and of all the lags of each variable; AIC with lags minus",
                               "without"))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, T_lags_p_common, P_lags_p_common, equal_T_p, equal_P_p, aic_common_vs_no_lags,
         aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  mutate(aic_common_vs_unrestricted = aic_common_vs_no_lags - aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  select(-aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each variable;",
                               "test that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag (in",
                               "the unrestricted model); AIC against no lags and against the",
                               "unrestricted lags"))

significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r deviation-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
LAG_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "TM", 3, 3L, "TM", -3, 3L, "TM", -3, 1L,
  "RR", -3, 1L, "RR", -3, 2L, "RR", 3, 1L
)
plot_lag_paths <- function(effects, version) {
  effects %>%
    semi_join(LAG_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    mutate(
      cell = sprintf("%s %+d SD at %s", VARIABLE_LABELS[variable], deviation, level),
      cell = factor(cell, levels = unique(cell)),
      main_panel = panel == main$label,
      panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),
      across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x)
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(through, estimate, colour = panel)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(data = function(x) filter(x, main_panel),
                aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), fill = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], alpha = 0.12,
                colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    facet_wrap(~cell, nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = stats::setNames(GRID_PALETTE[seq_along(lag_fits)],
                                                 vapply(lag_fits, function(x) x$panel$label, "")),
                        name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Years after the deviation", y = "Cumulative effect on GDP per capita (pp)",
         title = paste("Cumulative effect of a +/-3 SD year over the following years:",
                       version),
         subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, five lags; ",
                           "band: 95% CI for ", main$label, ".")) +
    theme_results()
}
plot_lag_paths(lag_effects, "unrestricted lags")
plot_lag_paths(common_effects, "common interaction")
```

## Ten lags, common interaction

The common-interaction model with the deviations of the previous ten years,
against the model without lags on the same rows (the ERA5 panels then start in
1970: a 20-year precipitation deviation needs climate from 20 years before).
The confidence intervals of the cumulative effects use the full clustered
covariance of all the lag coefficients.

```{r ten-lags}
N_LAGS_LONG <- 10L
common_long_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit, N_LAGS_LONG)
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", N_LAGS_LONG), restricted_terms("RR", N_LAGS_LONG),
                    CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, model = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(mr),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      aic_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0)
    )
  )
}

long_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), common_long_lags)
long_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$model, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE, n_lags = N_LAGS_LONG)
}))

bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(T_lags_p, P_lags_p), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         aic_vs_no_lags = round(aic_vs_no_lags, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each",
                               "variable; AIC minus the model without lags on the same rows"))

significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == 5)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through five years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == N_LAGS_LONG)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through ten years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r ten-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
plot_lag_paths(long_effects, "ten lags, common interaction") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:N_LAGS_LONG) +
  labs(subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, ten lags; ",
                         "band: 95% CI for ", main$label, " (full clustered covariance of the ",
                         "lag coefficients)."))
```

# Growth outliers: none, non-weather or all dropped

The preferred model on every panel with no growth outlier dropped, with the
outliers whose cause does not involve weather dropped (the main sample), and
with all of them dropped (the weather-driven ones too). The same country-years
in every panel. For each: the joint tests, the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in
the year, and the cumulative effects of the dry and hot tails (five
unrestricted lags; ten lags with the common interaction).

```{r outlier-samples}
OUTLIER_SAMPLES <- list(
  "none dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL[0, ],
  "non-weather dropped" = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
  "all dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL
)
outlier_fit <- function(panel, sample) {
  drop <- OUTLIER_SAMPLES[[sample]]
  keep <- !paste(panel$all$GID_0, panel$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  d <- add_deviation_terms(panel$all[keep, ], PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  list(panel = modifyList(panel, list(label = paste0(panel$label, " | ", sample))),
       data = d, preferred = fit_model(preferred_terms, d),
       source_panel = panel$label, sample = sample)
}
all_panels <- c(national_panels, list(dose))
outlier_fits <- unlist(lapply(all_panels, function(p) {
  lapply(names(OUTLIER_SAMPLES), function(s) outlier_fit(p, s))
}), recursive = FALSE)

bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample, rows = stats::nobs(f$preferred),
                 temperature_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devRR"))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms by outlier sample")

significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, climate_effects))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in the year (pp) by outlier sample;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# Dry and hot tails: in the year, and cumulative with lags.
TAIL_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell, ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "RR", -3, 1L,
  "P -3 SD, 1.5 m", "RR", -3, 2L,
  "T +3 SD, 25 °C", "TM", 3, 3L
)
tail_summary <- function(f) {
  d5 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 5L)
  lags5 <- unlist(lapply(1:5, function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m5 <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, lags5), d5)
  d10 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 10L)
  m10 <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", 10L), restricted_terms("RR", 10L), CONTROLS), d10)
  effects <- bind_rows(
    mutate(climate_effects(f), horizon = "year"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m5, f$panel$label, FALSE, 5L), through == 5), horizon = "5 years"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m10, f$panel$label, TRUE, 10L), through == 10),
           horizon = "10 years")
  )
  effects %>%
    inner_join(TAIL_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    transmute(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample,
              column = paste0(cell, ": ", horizon),
              value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = value)
}
bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, tail_summary)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Dry and hot tails by outlier sample (pp of GDP per capita): in the",
                               "year, cumulative over five years (unrestricted lags) and ten years",
                               "(common interaction); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```
